claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Heading at the wrong level: the transcription's convention is one '#' per numbering component (7. is '#', 7.1 '##', 6.4.1 '###', 6.4.2.1 '####', 6.4.2.1.1 '#####'); should be '#####'.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page shows the heading '6.4.2.3.1 Definition of Imperative Statement' and the markdown carries it word for word; nothing is missing. The claimed convention does not hold in this part of the transcription. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md, 6.4.2 'Statements and Sentences' is '###' (line 7623), 6.4.2.1/6.4.2.2/6.4.2.3/6.4.2.4 are '###' or '####' (6.4.2.3 is '###' at line 7701), and the sibling five-component headings 6.4.2.1.2, 6.4.2.2.1, 6.4.2.2.2 and 6.4.2.3.2 are all '####'. 6.4.2.3.1 at '####' nests correctly one level below its parent 6.4.2.3 ('###') and matches its sibling 6.4.2.3.2. The only outlier nearby is 6.4.2.1.1 at '#####', which is not on this page. This is a Markdown heading-depth formatting choice, not a content discrepancy against the PDF.
